stimuli.title: Pia, Nisha, Isha, Kiran, Esha, Hema, Uma, Sana occupy eight flats on floors 1 (bottom) to 4 (top). Each floor has Flat A to the west of Flat B. Each flat has one resident. For ordering only, count Floor 1 A, Floor 1 B, Floor 2 A, Floor 2 B, and so on.
stimuli.body:
Use all the following clues:
• Isha occupies floor 1, flat A.
• The floor numbers of Esha and Uma differ by 1.
• Nisha lives above Uma.
• Pia and Uma occupy flats with the same letter on different floors.
• Kiran lives below Hema.
• Nisha and Uma occupy flats with different letters.
• Hema lives in Flat A.
• Nisha and Esha occupy flats with different letters.
• Esha lives below Sana.
• Pia and Kiran live on the same floor.

Statements: Only a few cheques are loans. Some loans are coins. All coins are bonds.
Conclusions:
I. All cheques are bonds.
II. No loans is a bonds.
questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. A need not be contained in D. Some B are C and therefore D, contradicting II.

questions.stem:
Statements: Some cheques are loans. All loans are coins. No coins is a bonds.
Conclusions:
I. Some cheques are coins.
II. Some loans are bonds.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only I follows. The stated A–B overlap lies in C. Since B is contained in C, no B can be D.

questions.stem:
Statements: No cheques is a loans. Some loans are coins. All coins are bonds.
Conclusions:
I. All cheques are bonds.
II. Some bonds are loans.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only II follows. The B–C overlap is inside D, proving II. No universal A–D relation is given.

questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few cheques are loans. All loans are coins. No coins is a bonds.
Conclusions:
I. Some cheques are not loans.
II. No loans is a bonds.
questions.explanation: Answer: Both I and II follow. Only a few means some are and some are not. All B are C and no C is D excludes every B from D.

Conclusions: I. X < T   II. X ≤ R.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is not guaranteed; II is not guaranteed. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.stem:
In a substitution language, each word has one distinct code. Code order is arbitrary.
credit growth banking = ni pa ze
credit rural digital = vo ze lu
growth rural secure = ni vo mi
banking digital secure = mi pa lu
credit growth secure = ni ze mi
What is the code for “growth”?
questions.explanation: Answer: ni. Compare the intersections of the coded lines. The complete consistent mapping is: credit = ze, growth = ni, banking = pa, rural = vo, digital = lu, secure = mi.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 41 km south, turns left and walks 36 km, then turns left and walks 14 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 45. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 27 km along the initial direction and 36 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(27² + 36²) = 45 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 101 km south, turns right and walks 228 km, then turns right and walks 6 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 247. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 95 km along the initial direction and 228 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(95² + 228²) = 247 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 30 km south, turns left and walks 60 km, then turns left and walks 5 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 65. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 25 km along the initial direction and 60 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(25² + 60²) = 65 km.

questions.stem: C is the mother of G. E is the son of G. F is the father of G. How is E related to F?
questions.explanation: Answer: Grandson. F is a parent of G, and E is G’s son. Hence E is F’s grandchild.

questions.stem: A is the brother of F. F is the mother of B. G is the father of A and F. How is A related to B?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. A is the brother of B’s mother F. Therefore A is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: G is the only daughter of E. E is the father of G. C is the son of G. F is the sister of E. How is E related to C?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. E is the father of G, and G is C’s mother. Thus E is the maternal grandfather.

questions.stem: In a queue of 56 candidates, a candidate is 13th from the front. After moving 3 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 41. New front rank = 13+3 = 16. Back rank = 56 − 16 + 1 = 41.

questions.stem: In a queue of 41 candidates, a candidate is 13th from the front. After moving 4 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 25. New front rank = 13+4 = 17. Back rank = 41 − 17 + 1 = 25.

questions.stem: An item costs ₹1800. It is marked above cost and sold at a 10% discount on marked price, earning 25% profit. Find the marked price (₹, to two decimals).
questions.explanation: Answer: 2500. Selling price = 1800 × 125/100. Marked price = selling price ÷ 0.9 = 2500.

questions.stem: A can finish a job in 26 days and B in 39 days. They work together for 4 days, then B leaves. How many more days does A need? (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 19.33. Use 78 work units. Rates: A = 3, B = 2 units/day. Remaining = 78 − 4×5. Divide by A’s rate 3.

questions.stem: A boat travels 285 km downstream and the same distance upstream. Its still-water speed is 17 km/h and stream speed is 2 km/h. Find the total time (hours).
A invests ₹26000 for 12 months. B invests ₹78000 for 8 months. Total profit is ₹93600. Find B’s share (₹).
questions.explanation: Answer: 62400. Capital-time ratio = 12 : 24. B’s share = total × 24/(36) = 62400.

questions.stem: What is the difference (₹) between compound interest and simple interest on ₹22000 at 15% per annum for 2 years, compounded annually?
questions.explanation: Answer: 495. For 2 years, CI − SI = P(r/100)² = 22000 × (15/100)².

questions.stem: A vessel contains 95 litres of milk and water in ratio 3:2. How many litres of pure milk must be added to make the ratio 2:1?
questions.explanation: Answer: 19. Milk = 3V/5, water = 2V/5. Solve (3V/5 + x)/(2V/5) = 2; x = V/5 = 19.

questions.stem: The average of 32 numbers is 48. One number, 60, is replaced and the average rises by 5. What is the new number?
questions.explanation: Answer: 220. Total increases by 32 × 5. New number = 60 + 160.

questions.stem: A father is three times as old as his daughter. After 5 years, their combined age will be 74 years. Find the father’s present age.
questions.explanation: Answer: 48. Let daughter’s age be x. Father is 3x. 4x + 10 = 74; x = 16, so father = 48.
